items.title: MARKET PULSE PM JULY 31, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed higher, outperforming most regional markets as investors rotated into consumer and plantation stocks despite weaker Wall Street cues. The market was supported by selective buying in defensive and commodity-linked sectors. In the crypto market, Bitcoin fell to RM260,049.

items.title: Iran strikes two tankers attempting Hormuz transit under US escort
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Friday that they had struck two tankers attempting to pass though the strategic Strait of Hormuz under the "air escort" of the US military. The IRGC said the "non-compliant oil tankers... were struck and brought to a halt, while four other oil tankers quickly changed course and returned to their previous positions." On Thursday, the Guards said two oil tankers attempting to transit the Strait had turned back after one caught fire.--AFP © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Four bodies recovered after Pakistan avalanche traps Nirmal Purja expedition
items.summary: SKARDU, Pakistan: Search teams found four bodies near the site of an avalanche in northern Pakistan that left 10 people missing from a climbing expedition led by renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja, police said on Friday. The Alpine Club of Pakistan said the expedition comprised 10 people – including five Nepalese, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American, and a climber from China. "The Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) has received deeply concerning reports of an avalanche that struck a team of climbers on Broad Peak (8,047m) in the Karakoram mountain range," the club said late on Thursday.

items.title: SME's strong 2025 performance reflects resilience amid global uncertainties – Samenta
items.summary: The Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) national president Datuk William Ng said the local SMEs have continued to invest, innovate and expand their reach into regional and international markets, and as a result, SME exports surged 10.5 per cent to RM214.5 billion. "To sustain this momentum and reach our national target of a 40 per cent gross domestic product (GDP) contribution, we must ensure that unnecessary regulatory hurdles do not bog down our SMEs. According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), MSMEs achieved a 5.7 per cent GDP growth in 2025, outpacing the broader national economy's 5.2 per cent growth over the same period.

items.title: Hamas: Israel must honour Gaza deal before disarmament
items.summary: CAIRO: Implementation of the deal to bring peace to Gaza announced by US President Donald Trump will depend on Israel first meeting its commitments under an agreement reached last year, a senior Hamas official told Reuters on Friday. Ghazi Hamad, a Hamas official involved in the negotiations, said the agreement was a "comprehensive framework" that went beyond the issue of disarmament and would depend on Israel implementing the first phase of an agreement hammered out last year in the Egyptian resort of Sharm el-Sheikh. On Thursday, an Israeli official said Israel would not agree to withdraw behind the so-called Yellow Line before Hamas is disarmed and the Gaza Strip is demilitarised.--REUTERS © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Ringgit ends week marginally higher against US dollar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended the week marginally higher against the US dollar following weaker-than-expected US economic data although sentiment towards the greenback remained firm, as expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike in September stayed intact. At 6pm, the local currency appreciated to 4.0835/0875 versus the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0875/0930. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said expectations of a September interest rate hike by the Fed stayed intact despite weaker US economic data, helping to limit the US dollar's losses.

items.title: Hamas agrees to disarm under Trump Gaza plan, Israel yet to respond
items.summary: GAZA CITY, Palestinian Territories: Hamas said Friday it had agreed to a deal announced by US President Donald Trump to end the war with Israel, that includes it handing over its weapons to a Palestinian governing committee and the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza. Israel did not immediately comment on the announcement, but shortly beforehand an Israeli political source had told AFP the proposed agreement did not "satisfactorily" address Israeli demands for the full demilitarisation of the Gaza Strip. Hamas officials told AFP that a committee established by Trump's Board of Peace to govern Gaza would oversee the process of storing the movement's weapons.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia ends higher on blue-chip buying, tracks most regional markets
items.summary: Among the heavyweights, Maybank added two sen to RM10.90, Public Bank perked up one sen to RM5.17, CIMB added six sen to RM7.89, IHH Healthcare was unchanged to RM8.35, while Tenaga Nasional fell two sen to RM14.60. As for the active stocks, Zetrix AI put on three sen to 74.5 sen, Nationgate climbed six sen to RM1.19, V.S Industry edged up one sen each to 23 sen, TWL inched up half-a-sen to 2.5 sen, and Inari Amertron increased 10 sen to RM2.22. Hong Leong Industries led the losers list, falling 28 sen to RM17.72, Allianz Malaysia lost 20 sen to RM21.00, Kuala Lumpur Kepong eased 18 sen to RM21.02, Concrete Engineering Products slid 14 sen to RM3.32, and MISC fell 13 sen to RM7.99.

items.title: Police confirm three fatalities, two injuries in multiple RXZ‑related motorcycle accidents across Pahang
items.summary: KUANTAN, July 31 — Three motorcyclists were killed and two others injured in four separate accidents in Pahang linked to the RXZ Members 8.0 gathering at the Gong Badak Motorsports Circuit in Kuala Nerus, Terengganu. Temerloh district police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police received information about the accident at 11pm, involving a Yamaha LC135 motorcycle rider who was travelling from Klang, Selangor, to Terengganu to attend the gathering. “The victim was believed to have lost control and fallen onto the left lane before being thrown onto the right lane.

items.title: CAAM probing if there were security lapses before pilot's departure to Indonesia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) is investigating whether there were any regulatory or security lapses which led to a Malaysian pilot departing Malaysia, and later being detained in Indonesia, over alleged drug smuggling. CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said they are aware of the reported incident involving the Malaysian pilot and was currently gathering the relevant facts. "The matter will be investigated from a regulatory perspective, including the airline's compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and the airport operator's security processes, to determine whether there were any lapses prior to his departure from Malaysia," Norazman said.

items.title: E&O to acquire prime Jalan Kia Peng site with Majestic Gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Eastern & Oriental Bhd (E&O) and Majestic Gen Sdn Bhd are acquiring a prime freehold site along Jalan Kia Peng, strengthening E&O's premium development landbank in Kuala Lumpur. The acquisition will be undertaken through KP Urban Sdn Bhd, which is 66.67 per cent owned by E&O subsidiary KCB Holdings Sdn Bhd and 33.33 per cent by Golden Urban Nite Sdn Bhd, an affiliate of Majestic Gen. E&O and Majestic Gen plan to develop the site into a signature high-rise residential project, combining E&O's placemaking expertise with Majestic Gen's development capabilities to create a premium residential address.

items.title: SCIB secures RM11.9mil EPCC contract in Sabah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak Consolidated Industries Bhd (SCIB) has secured a RM11.9 million engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) subcontract for upgrading works at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS). In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, SCIB said the contract was awarded to its wholly owned subsidiary, SCIB Industrialised Building System Sdn Bhd (SIBS), by Demi Cerah Construction Sdn Bhd. SCIB non-independent non-executive chairman Datuk Chong Loong Men said the contract further strengthens the group's construction and EPCC portfolio while expanding its presence in Sabah.

items.title: #NSTviral: RXZ Members 8.0: Divided views after Gambang petrol station congestion
items.summary: The user claimed the gathering disrupted motorists and called for such events to be stopped. A user said many participants were educated, working people and that the gathering was simply a shared hobby. This is just their hobby," the user said.

items.title: PM pledges increased allocation for Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia in upcoming Budget to aid low‑income families
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 31 — The government will increase its allocation for Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM) in the upcoming Budget as part of its continued commitment to helping low-income families, particularly women, improve their economic well-being, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the government would enhance its support for AIM while maintaining the special allocation already provided to the agency. The prime minister also said the government would increase Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) assistance in the upcoming Budget.

items.title: Penang drug raids lead to three arrests, discovery of smoke grenades
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Police crippled a drug trafficking syndicate, seizing various drugs and two smoke hand grenades during coordinated raids that led to the arrest of three suspects. Seberang Prai Tengah district police chief Assistant Commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said the first raid was carried out by the district police Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department at a house in Taman Gemilang Indah here at about 6.40pm on Thursday, following intelligence on suspected drug trafficking activities. "Police also found an iron box containing two smoke hand grenades concealed inside a kitchen cabinet," he said today.

items.title: Malaysian embassy seeks consular access to pilot detained in Indonesia
items.summary: JAKARTA: The Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta is seeking consular access to a Malaysian pilot detained in Indonesia on alleged drug trafficking offences following his arrest at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport earlier this week. The embassy said it had received official notification from Indonesia's Directorate of Drug Crimes under the National Police Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) regarding the detention of the Malaysian national at Terminal 3 of the airport. "The embassy respects Indonesia's legal process and is engaging with the Indonesian authorities to obtain consular access to the Malaysian citizen concerned," the embassy said in a statement on Friday.

items.title: High Court allows prosecution appeal, sets aside Papagomo’s acquittal in sedition case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — The High Court today set aside the sessions court’s acquittal of political influencer Wan Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, on a sedition charge and directed him to enter his defence. Justice Nurulhuda Nur’aini Nor delivered the ruling after allowing the prosecution’s appeal against the September 3, 2025 decision that freed Wan Azri without his defence being called, Free Malaysia Today reported. Wan Azri was also allowed bail of RM7,000.

items.title: Wife of missing pastor appeals to Anwar over probe stay
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The wife of missing Pastor Raymond Koh has appealed directly to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to intervene after the Court of Appeal stayed a High Court order requiring police to recommence investigations into her husband's 2017 disappearance. In a heartfelt letter, Susanna Liew said she was appealing to Anwar because time was of the essence in the investigation into her husband's disappearance. Liew is seeking immediate intervention after the Court of Appeal on July 29 dismissed her application to lift the stay on investigations ordered by the High Court.

items.title: Penang police bust Japan travel scam call centre in luxury condominium
items.summary: Northeast district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the Criminal Investigation Division of the Northeast district police headquarters (IPD) and Tanjung Tokong police station at 4.45 pm also arrested seven foreign men and a foreign woman aged between 25 and 37. Abdul Rozak said investigations found that the syndicate was offering travel packages to Japan online, targeting victims in China and Taiwan. He said the police would continue to intensify operations to combat criminal activities masterminded by foreigners, especially involving online fraud syndicates.

items.title: Senator files police report over video alleging DAP is a communist party, calls content ‘malicious and baseless’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — DAP senator Dr RA Lingeshwaran has filed a police report against a video circulating on social media that alleges the party is a communist organisation. “DAP is not a communist party and is not founded on any communist ideology,” Lingeshwaran said, stressing that the party is multiracial, upholds the Federal Constitution and supports Malaysia’s parliamentary system. Lingeshwaran argued the video was designed to provoke hatred, damage the party’s reputation and inflame racial tensions.

items.title: Unisem Q2 net profit rises 8.5pct on stronger sales volumes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Unisem (M) Bhd's net profit rose 8.5 per cent to RM9.91 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, from RM9.13 million a year earlier, as revenue increased 20 per cent to RM570.12 million from RM475.15 million. For the first half of the financial year, however, Unisem slipped into a net loss of RM3.45 million from a net profit of RM15.14 million a year earlier despite recording higher revenue. First-half revenue rose 14.6 per cent to RM1.03 billion from RM898.77 million in the corresponding period last year.

items.title: Papagomo acquittal set aside, High Court orders defence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today ordered blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris to enter his defence on a charge of making seditious remarks by alleging that the current government was pro-Israel. Judge Nurulhuda Nur'Aini Mohamad Nor allowed the prosecution's appeal and overturned the Sessions Court's earlier decision to acquit Wan Azri. She ordered Wan Azri to enter his defence before the same Sessions Court judge, Siti Aminah Ghazali.

items.title: Indonesian artiste fined RM500 for airport outburst, pleads guilty to drug charge
items.summary: SEPANG: Indonesian actor and model Samudera Hurley Taylor was fined RM500 by the magistrate's court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of using insulting words against airline staff members and disobeying orders from authorities at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). On the first charge, he was fined the maximum RM400 for disobeying lawful orders issued by auxiliary police officers. For a second charge, Samudera was fined RM100 for causing public disturbance by behaving in a disorderly manner.

items.title: Malaysian Embassy seeks consular access to pilot arrested over 25kg Jakarta drug haul
items.summary: JAKARTA, July 31 — The Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta is seeking consular access to a Malaysian pilot detained in Indonesia on alleged drug trafficking offences following his arrest at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport earlier this week. The embassy said it had received official notification from Indonesia’s Directorate of Drug Crimes under the National Police Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) regarding the detention of the Malaysian national at Terminal 3 of the airport. “The Embassy respects Indonesia’s legal process and is engaging with the Indonesian authorities to obtain consular access to the Malaysian citizen concerned,” the embassy said in a statement on Friday.

items.title: Chong Chieng Jen files appeal against ‘black hole’ ruling permitting govt defamation suits, says decision against public interest
items.summary: KUCHING, July 31 — Sarawak Democratic Action Party (DAP) chairman Chong Chieng Jen has decided to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision against him in the ‘black hole’ case. “The Court of Appeal has, inter alia, decided that, in Malaysia, a government can sue its citizen for defamation. On July 3, the Court of Appeal here dismissed Chong’s appeal against the High Court’s ruling in the 2013 ‘black hole’ defamation suit and doubled the damages awarded.

items.title: Accountability, enforcement key to curb illegal cigarette trade: Coffee shops association
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Singapore Coffee Shop Proprietors' General Association (MSCSPGA) has called for sustained enforcement against the illegal cigarette trade and greater transparency through the public release of the Health Ministry's registry of legally registered cigarette brands. According to the association, such abuses have allowed the illegal cigarette trade to operate openly at the retail level, with foreign workers increasingly being used to sell illicit cigarettes. "The growing presence of illicit cigarette sales involving foreign workers not only harms legitimate retailers, but also exposes illegal practices that allow the illicit trade to thrive.

items.title: UNHCR cardholders subject to Malaysian laws, says Immigration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Holders of valid United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards are still regarded as illegal immigrants, but are exempted from prosecution under the Immigration Act 1959/63 for offences of overstaying and entering the country without valid travel documents, according to the Immigration Department. Apart from these exemptions, UNHCR cardholders remain subject to Malaysian laws, the department said in a statement to Bernama today. Immigration said the public should not take matters into their own hands against foreigners, as doing so could have implications for security, public order and the law.

items.title: ‘Let you die here’: Plumber gets eight years’ jail for attempted murder of 16‑year‑old girl in Penampang
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 31 — A plumber was sentenced to eight years in prison by the Sessions Court here for attempting to murder a teenage girl two months ago. The accused was charged with using a knife to stab the undocumented teenager, 16, in the neck inside a toilet of an unnumbered house in Penampang on May 7. The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor DK Afiqah Alya Ak Johari @ Pg Johari.

items.title: Johari urges investors to build with Malaysia, not simply sell to it
items.summary: TANJONG MALIM, July 31 — Foreign investments brought into Malaysia must deliver tangible benefits to the national economy, including helping to strengthen the trade surplus, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He noted that the country’s import value has reached RM1.45 trillion. It must grow.

items.title: Malaysia must accelerate charging infrastructure to drive EV adoption, minister says
items.summary: TANJONG MALIM, July 31 — The electric vehicle industry’s development should not focus solely on vehicle sales but must be supported by a comprehensive ecosystem, said Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He said this ecosystem includes developing local technology, building a skilled workforce, and establishing an adequate network of public charging stations. Johari said that while hybrid technology is not new, Proton has managed to make it more affordable for the public.

items.title: Neighbour recalls quiet family after mother, daughters found dead
items.summary: IPOH: A neighbour of a woman and her two young daughters, who were found dead at their home in Bandar Baru Tambun here last night, described them as a quiet family who kept mostly to themselves. The neighbour, who wished to be known only as Siti, 60, said the family had lived in the area for about 10 years and were rarely seen outside their home except for routine activities. She said she last saw the family during her child's wedding, where they attended as guests.

items.title: Malaysia's population grows, 12 states hit ageing status
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's population is estimated to increase by 0.5 per cent to 34.4 million in 2026, up from 34.2 million in 2025. At the state level, Terengganu recorded the highest population growth rate at 1.2 per cent, surpassing the national average, followed by Kelantan (1.0 per cent), Selangor (0.6 per cent), Putrajaya (0.6 per cent) and Pahang (0.6 per cent). "Selangor continues to record the largest share of the population in 2026 at 21.7 per cent, followed by Johor (12.3 per cent) and Sabah (11.0 per cent), while Labuan and Putrajaya recorded the smallest population shares at 0.3 per cent and 0.4 per cent respectively," DOSM said in a statement today.

items.title: UNHCR cards do not confer legal immigration status in Malaysia, department says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Holders of valid United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards are still regarded as illegal immigrants, but are exempted from prosecution under the Immigration Act 1959/63 for offences of overstaying and entering the country without valid travel documents, according to the Immigration Department (JIM). In a statement to Bernama today, the department said that apart from these exemptions, UNHCR cardholders remain subject to Malaysian laws. JIM also stressed that the public should not take matters into their own hands against foreign nationals, as doing so could have implications for security, public order and the law.

items.title: Ilham Centre: Malay vote consolidation gives BN-PN advantage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) are poised to wrest control of Negri Sembilan with at least 22 seats in tomorrow's election, with a two-thirds majority also within reach, according to Ilham Centre. "Overall, Ilham Centre's projection shows that BN and PN collectively have the potential to control 22 state seats and form a stable majority bloc, while PH is expected to win a minimum of nine seats," it said in a statement today. Ilham said cooperation between BN and PN had also translated into stronger-than-expected vote transfers between supporters of the two parties.

items.title: Negri polls: Anwar confident of PH victory, focus on stability
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he is confident the coalition can secure victory in tomorrow's polls. Asked for his forecast of PH's performance in the Negri Sembilan election, Anwar said the coalition would focus on doing its best. When asked how many seats Pakatan Harapan expects to win, Anwar declined to give a figure, saying: "You'll have to ask Aminuddin (Negri Sembilan caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun)."

items.title: RXZ gathering tragedy: Three riders killed in Pahang crashes
items.summary: KUANTAN: Three motorcyclists heading to the RXZ Members 8.0 gathering in Kuala Terengganu were killed, while two others were injured in four separate crashes across Pahang within 12 hours. The crashes occurred between 10.10pm yesterday and 10.10am today in Maran, Temerloh and Rompin, involving riders travelling to the annual motorcycle gathering. Maran district police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said the first crash occurred at 6.30am when Mohd Fauzi Othman, 44, lost control of his motorcycle at Km184.9 of LPT1 while travelling with friends from Kuala Lumpur to Kuala Terengganu.

items.title: Malaysia's AI push drives growth, opens doors in UAE
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly becoming central to economic growth, productivity and competitiveness, industry insiders said. Malaysia's AI policies, including the National AI Roadmap, position AI as a cross-sector technology to accelerate digital transformation across industries and the public sector. "Malaysia is building up on AI across all sectors.

items.title: Private sector credit growth holds steady in June
items.summary: Credit to the private non-financial sector expanded 6.4 per cent in June, supported by sustained growth in both outstanding loans, which increased 6.0 per cent, and corporate bonds, which rose 8.1 per cent. Business loan growth strengthened to 7.2 per cent from 7.0 per cent in May, driven mainly by lending to non-small and medium enterprises, particularly for working capital. Outstanding household loans grew 5.3 per cent, slightly slower than the 5.5 per cent recorded in May, amid moderating growth in personal use loans.

items.title: Anwar says Tabung Haji RCI report released in full, without redactions
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the full Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the management and operations of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) had been released in full without any censorship or redactions. The Prime Minister’s Department did not remove any part of the report. We published the entire report, including the recommendations and the processes that took place.

items.title: USM appoints Noor Hazlina as deputy vice-chancellor
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) has appointed Professor Datin Dr Noor Hazlina Ahmad as its new deputy vice-chancellor (Academic and International), effective Aug 3. Noor Hazlina, an academic specialising in entrepreneurship, innovation, leadership and organisational development, holds a PhD in Entrepreneurship from the University of Adelaide, a Master of Business Administration from USM and a Bachelor of Science in Humanities (Psychology) from the International Islamic University Malaysia. Before her appointment, she served as dean of the USM School of Management since 2019, where she led strategic initiatives to strengthen academic excellence, internationalisation and institutional sustainability.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI report: Anwar questions 13-month bonus payout, calls it breach of trust
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described the alleged payment of 13 months’ worth of bonuses to Tabung Haji staff despite the institution recording losses as a breach of trust. The issue was among several concerns raised in the Tabung Haji inquiry report, The Star reported today. He said such payments were among the many issues highlighted in the report, questioning how a loss-making institution could justify rewarding employees in such a manner.

items.title: Kuching High Court reduces Bau man’s jail term for sexually assaulting teen stepdaughter to 18 years
items.summary: This reduced the 54-year-old’s total imprisonment term from 54 years to 18 years. He was previously sentenced by the Kuching Sessions Court on October 31, 2025 to a total of 54 years’ imprisonment and 24 strokes of the cane. The Sessions Court imposed 18 years’ imprisonment for each of the three charges and ordered the sentences to run consecutively.

items.title: Citadel buys most of Situational's stock holdings after AI share rout, sources say
items.summary: NEW YORK: Situational Awareness, an AI-focused hedge fund run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, sold the bulk of its stock portfolio to Ken Griffin's Citadel after being battered by heavy losses in its tech holdings, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday. Situational held positions in several prominent tech names including Broadcom, Intel, and CoreWeave, according to its most recent regulatory filings. Aschenbrenner blamed short sellers who targeted the firm's positions for exacerbating losses, the report said.

items.title: Syerleena condemns dog's killing, calls for transparent probe
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Bukit Bendera member of parliament Syerleena Abdul Rashid has condemned the killing of a dog known as Rocky and called for a swift, transparent and independent investigation into the incident. Syerleena said in a statement today that the brutal killing of Rocky, described as a pet and a beloved companion, had shocked Malaysians and left a grieving family mourning the loss of a cherished animal. "As a Malay Muslim, I reject without hesitation the brutal killing of Rocky," she said.

items.title: Warisan denies organising solidarity rally for Shafie Apdal in Kota Kinabalu, files police report over fake posters
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 31 — Parti Warisan (Warisan) has denied allegations it is organising a solidarity rally for president Datuk Seri Panglima Mohd Shafie Apdal at Padang Merdeka here on Sunday (August 2). Warisan secretary-general Loretto S. Padua Jr said the party has lodged a police report over the distribution of posters said to contain false information about the rally. Party members lodged the police report at the Kota Kinabalu Police Headquarters on Thursday evening.

items.title: Undecided voters and turnout take centre stage in Negeri Sembilan’s final campaign hours
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 31 — As the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election campaign enters its final hours, political coalitions and parties are intensifying their final campaign drive and strengthening their campaign operations ahead of tomorrow’s vote. Contesting parties have turned their attention to winning over undecided voters and boosting turnout before the campaign period officially ends at 11.59pm tonight. Negeri Sembilan Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said the coalition’s campaign machinery would continue its ground efforts ahead of polling, focusing especially on key areas identified as crucial.

items.title: Rapid KL extends free rides on LRT3 Shah Alam line until Aug 14
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Rapid KL will extend its free service period for the LRT3 Shah Alam line until August 14, 2026, to allow more users to experience the new public transport service connecting Petaling Jaya, Shah Alam and Klang. In a statement today, Rapid KL said the extension would give commuters more time to familiarise themselves with the new system while encouraging greater use of public transport for daily travel. Rapid KL said the initiative was also aimed at helping reduce daily travel costs while building public confidence in the efficiency and comfort of the country’s public transport system.

items.title: A nation is defended not only at its borders, Grand Imam tells worshippers at Masjid Negara on Warriors’ Day
items.summary: Delivering the Friday sermon in conjunction with Warriors’ Day titled Setia Pada Amanah, Teguh Mempertahankan Negara (Faithful to Trust, Steadfast in Defending the Nation), he reminded worshippers that national sovereignty and peace are safeguarded every day through the fulfilment of responsibilities by every segment of society. In reality, the nation is defended every day through the fulfilment of responsibilities by its people. Among those present were Chief of Defence Forces Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman, Chief of Navy Adm Tan Sri Zulhelmy Ithnain and Chief of Air Force Gen Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris.

items.title: SPAN says Malaysia’s water supplies should hold through 2026, with risks ahead
items.summary: PADANG BESAR, July 31 — The National Water Services Commission (SPAN) is strengthening its preparedness to face the Super El Nino phenomenon expected to occur in November through continuous monitoring of dams and water treatment plants (WTP) nationwide to ensure that water supply to consumers continues to be guaranteed. SPAN Emergency and Risk Preparedness Committee (JKKR) chairman Sulaiman Kamisan said his party, together with related agencies, also conducted working visits to several dams in Kedah and Perlis to assess the current situation of raw water sources. Meanwhile, he said Perlis is among the states currently receiving attention due to the water level of Timah Tasoh Dam being at a critical level.

items.title: Death sentence stands for former Army pathologist Kunaseegaran convicted of killing DPP Kevin Morais
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 31 — The Federal Court today upheld the death sentence imposed on former Army pathologist Colonel R. Kunaseegaran for the murder of Deputy Public Prosecutor Datuk Kevin Morais after dismissing his application to review the apex court’s earlier decision affirming his conviction and sentence. Delivering the unanimous decision, Justice Hashim said Kunaseegaran, 63, had withdrawn his appeal against sentence during the earlier Federal Court proceedings, leaving no issue for the court to determine in relation to the sentence. The court also dismissed Kunaseegaran’s contention that the earlier Federal Court panel had considered only issues relating to motive and defective charges.

items.title: Saudi carrier Riyadh Air begins nonstop flights to Kuala Lumpur
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Riyadh Air has launched direct flights between Riyadh and Kuala Lumpur, making the Malaysian capital its first gateway into South-east Asia. In a statement today, the Saudi Arabian carrier said it began its inaugural Riyadh-Kuala Lumpur service on July 30 and will operate three weekly return flights between King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). “The new nonstop service marks a strategic expansion for Riyadh Air, strengthening connectivity between Saudi Arabia and Malaysia, one of South-east Asia’s most dynamic markets,” it said.

items.title: Govt shifts focus to scaling up MSMEs after resilient 2025, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Malaysia’s micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) sector remains resilient as the sector’s gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 5.7 per cent to almost RM690 billion in 2025. Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong said the growth outpaced the country’s economic growth of 5.2 per cent despite global uncertainties including geopolitical tensions. He said that almost 1.3 million MSMEs now account for 96 per cent of all businesses in Malaysia.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan polls: Anwar urges voters to turn out, give Pakatan mandate for stability and growth
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on Negeri Sembilan voters to come out and fulfil their responsibilities on polling day for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election tomorrow and to support Pakatan Harapan (PH) to continue the state’s agenda of stability and growth. He also called on Malay, Chinese, Indian and Orang Asli voters to fulfil their responsibilities on polling day to give PH a mandate to continue serving in ensuring stability and driving growth that will provide well-being to all the people of Negeri Sembilan together with the federal government and the Madani government. “I call on the residents and voters of Negeri Sembilan, especially the majority Muslim and our friends among the Chinese, Indians and Orang Asli, to exercise our responsibilities.

items.title: Police receive 87 reports, open 23 investigation papers in Negeri Sembilan election campaign
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 31 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) received 87 reports and opened 23 investigation papers involving alleged election offences during the campaign period for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election from July 18 until yesterday. Negeri Sembilan Police Chief DCP Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said 761 out of 787 permit applications submitted for ceramah and political campaign activities during the same period were approved. For the latest news on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9 .

items.title: Anwar sends well‑wishes to Sultan Ibrahim ahead of medical treatment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has offered prayers for the good health of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who is set to undergo medical treatment. “May His Majesty be blessed with continued good health and remain under the protection and mercy of Allah,” Anwar said in a Facebook post today. Earlier, Istana Negara announced that Sultan Ibrahim would undergo follow-up treatment for a musculoskeletal condition involving His Majesty’s back and hip.

items.title: Partial lane closures in Penang for LRT works on Jalan Kampung Relau, Tun Dr Awang from Aug 1
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 31 — Intermittent partial lane closures along Jalan Kampung Relau and Jalan Tun Dr. Awang will be implemented for 75 days from tomorrow to facilitate drainage and road widening works for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) Project. “The affected areas involve the leftmost lane in front of Penang International Commercial City (PICC) towards Bayan Lepas, the leftmost lane in front of the Petron Bukit Jambul petrol station heading towards Komtar and the leftmost lane from the Jalan Tun Dr. Awang entry slip road to Jalan Kampung Relau and SMK Sungai Nibong heading towards Komtar. MRT Corp said the closure was necessary to facilitate preliminary works under the Mutiara Line LRT Project’s CMC1 Package, involving drainage and road widening works.

items.title: Cyberjaya gets Malaysia’s first autonomous vehicle control centre ahead of Level 4 trials
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, July 31 — Malaysia’s first Remote Operations Centre (ROC) for autonomous logistics vehicles has been launched in Cyberjaya, paving the way for Level 4 autonomous vehicle trials on public roads. The facility at CoPlace 9 Cyberjaya was developed by Autonomous Logistic Solutions Sdn Bhd (ALS) in collaboration with the Selangor Information Technology & Digital Economy Corporation (Sidec) and Cyberview Sdn Bhd, and will support trials along the 22km Cyberjaya Malaysia Autonomous Vehicle (MyAV) Route. ALS managing director Alan Chong said the ROC would provide oversight for the company’s Level 4 autonomous logistics vehicle, the RoboVan, during upcoming trials.

items.title: Sabah JKR: Structural damage forces closure of Jalan Tun Fuad Stephen bridge in Kota Kinabalu
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 31 — The bridge at Kilometre 2.850 of Jalan Tun Fuad Stephen here will be closed from noon today after an inspection detected serious structural damage to its concrete deck. The Sabah Public Works Department (JKR), in a statement today, said the closure was necessary to ensure the safety of road users. “The closure affects the route from Kota Kinabalu City towards Teluk Likas and will be lifted once the temporary diversion works are completed.

items.title: Sarawak-level Warriors’ Day parade in Petra Jaya honours fallen heroes
items.summary: The 2026 Sarawak-level Warriors’ Day Parade, organised by the First Infantry Division of the Malaysian Army in collaboration with the Royal Malaysia Police Sarawak Contingent, brought together personnel from the armed forces, police, and veterans in honour of those who had defended the country’s sovereignty. Sarawak Governor Tun Pehin Sri Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar and his wife Toh Puan Datuk Patinggi Fauziah Mohd Sanusi graced the event, which was also attended by Minister for Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Dato Sri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah, who represented the Premier, Sarawak police commissioner CP Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, and First Infantry Division commander Maj Gen Mohd Sobirin Mohd Yusof. — Mohd Faisal Ahmad/The Borneo Post pic A total of 460 personnel from four detachments took part in the parade, led by commanding officer of the 10th Border Regiment Lt Col Ferry Shahrul Rizal Roslan, accompanied by the Combined Drum Platoon of the 4th Royal Armoured Corps Regiment, 13th Royal Malay Regiment Battalion and the 20th Royal Malay Regiment Battalion.

items.title: MACC receives four reports of alleged cash handouts in Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 31 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has received four reports related to alleged cash handouts during the Negeri Sembilan State Election. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the reports, received yesterday, involved two election candidates and two early voters. Abd Halim said the MACC would investigate whether the complaints contained elements of corruption or constituted election offences.
